item.title: Sydney sweats in spring hot spell, faces 'extreme' bushfire risk
item.description: Australia's most populous city Sydney baked in a burst of sweltering spring heat on Saturday, raising the risk of bushfires and prompting authorities to issue a ban on lighting fires.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's most populous city Sydney baked in a burst of sweltering spring heat on Saturday, raising the risk of bushfires and prompting authorities to issue a ban on lighting fires. The heat comes as a powerful El Nino [USN:P8N40Z06Q TEXT:"weather pattern"] in the Pacific, expected to be among the strongest in decades, drives hotter and drier conditions across southern Australia during the September-November spring season. On Saturday, the nation's weather forecaster said temperatures in the New South Wales capital, home to 5.6 million people, were set to hit 33 degrees Celsius (91.4 degrees Fahrenheit), nearly 13C above average. At Sydney Airport, the temperature was already 28.6C (83.48F) at 11:30 a.m. (0130 GMT)local time, more than seven degrees above the September mean maximum temperature, according to forecaster data. "Fresh to strong and gusty northwesterly winds developing during the morning, combined with dry, unseasonably warm conditions, will result in elevated fire dangers across the Greater Sydney Region today," the forecaster said. State fire authorities issued a total fire ban for Sydney where they rated fire risk as "extreme", the second highest danger rating. Climate change is causing extreme heat and fire weather to become more common in Australia, a bushfire-prone country of around 27 million. In January, thousands of firefighters [USN:L4N3YA1ME TEXT:"battled bushfires"] in the southeast that razed homes, cut power to thousands of homes and burned swathes of bushland.

item.title: Williams sisters' US Open return becomes celebration despite first-round exit
item.description: Four years after what seemed like their final bow, Serena and Venus Williams transformed a first-round U.S. Open doubles defeat into a celebration of tennis in front of 23,000 adoring fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Janina Rios
item.content:encoded: Four years after what seemed like their final bow, Serena and Venus Williams transformed a first-round U.S. Open doubles defeat into a celebration of tennis in front of 23,000 adoring fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Friday. Australia's Maya Joint and Taiwan's Chan Hao-ching emerged with a 6-3 6-7(6) 7-6(10-7) win, but for much of the contest the score felt irrelevant as fans roared at every Williams winner and fell into virtual silence at every point in between. Serena, 44, walked onto court wearing a shiny customized bomber jacket decorated with patches marking her U.S. Open singles and doubles triumphs. Her 46-year-old sister stodd alongside, the pair carrying matching pink bags. The comeback, which Serena said was at the suggestion of her daughter, carried the weight of more than two decades: 14 Grand Slam doubles titles together, two U.S. Open crowns, three Olympic gold medals, and another 30 Grand Slam singles titles between them. Joint and Chan, the 14th seeds, weathered the hostile atmosphere to take the opening set, but the Williams sisters hit back in the second, riding the crowd's energy to force a third set. The Americans showed they had lost none of their grit, going toe-to-toe with the younger pair, spurred on by a raucous crowd desperate to carry their long-time idols over the finish line. But Joint and Chan edged the super tiebreak in dramatic fashion, sealing victory in just over three hours. "Being able to play against such legends of the game is super special," said Joint on court. The reunion had been a long time coming. The sisters were forced to withdraw from the Wimbledon doubles draw after Serena suffered a knee injury in singles, leaving New York as the stage for the comeback fans had been waiting for. Joint, 20, beat Serena at Wimbledon in the only singles match of her comeback and the Australian struggled to sum up the Flushing Meadows experience. "I'm lost for words to think of it," she said. "She's my idol, both of them. I grew up in Michigan so I always looked up to them. Being able to play them twice is amazing." The Williams sisters had arrived in Flushing Meadows with little recent doubles form together, having lost in three sets to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in Cincinnati. Serena had already given New York a taste of the magic, though, teaming up with Carlos Alcaraz for a mixed doubles run that ended in the quarter-finals. Whether the sisters team up again is uncertain, so for the crowd at Flushing Meadows on Friday, seeing Serena's clenched fist and Venus at her side made it a night to remember.

item.title: Yankees OF Trent Grisham leaves game with apparent leg injury
item.description: New York Yankees center fielder Trent Grisham exited Friday night's game against the host San Diego Padres with an apparent hamstring injury after the top of the third inning.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New York Yankees center fielder Trent Grisham exited Friday night's game against the host San Diego Padres with an apparent hamstring injury after the top of the third inning. Grisham couldn't run down Xander Bogaerts' two-out fly ball into shallow left-center that fell for a single to score Ty France with the game's first run in the second. Before the Yankees took the field in the third, he was replaced by Heliot Ramos in the lineup with Spencer Jones switching from right to center field. Grisham walked in his only plate appearance in the second. He entered the game batting .211 with 18 homers and 59 RBIs. At the time he left the game, New York and San Diego were tied at 1-1. --Field Level Media

item.title: Yainer Diaz's homer helps rising Astros down Diamondbacks
item.description: Yainer Diaz homered, Cristian Javier matched his season high in strikeouts, and the Houston Astros claimed the opener of their three-game interleague series against the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks with a 3-1 victory on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Yainer Diaz homered, Cristian Javier matched his season high in strikeouts, and the Houston Astros claimed the opener of their three-game interleague series against the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks with a 3-1 victory on Friday. Javier (2-5) allowed one run on one hit with three walks and eight strikeouts in five innings. Josh Hader struck out the side in the ninth inning for his 23rd save of the season, making him the 41st player in history to record 250 career saves. The Astros (73-69) reached their top mark for games over .500 this season by winning for the seventh time in their past nine games. Houston improved to 4-1 on its current seven-game homestand. Arizona (74-68) took its fourth loss in five games. Diaz keyed the Astros' three-run third inning with a leadoff blast to left field off Merrill Kelly (9-13). The Houston catcher lined a 1-0 slider 383 feet for his 11th home run of the season and a 1-0 lead. Kelly responded by striking out LaMonte Wade Jr., but the Astros Jeremy Pena and Yordan Alvarez followed with singles. Isaac Paredes hit an RBI double, and Jose Altuve plated Alvarez with a sacrifice fly to left field, extending the Astros' advantage to 3-0. The third inning represented the lone hiccup for Kelly. He surrendered just two more hits, both singles, and did not allow another baserunner to reach scoring position. Kelly worked six innings, allowing three runs on seven hits and no walks while striking out four. Javier fanned a pair of batters in the top of the first inning and sidestepped a leadoff walk to Ketel Marte in the second. He struck out Corbin Carroll for a second time to strand Geraldo Perdomo at second in the third and added two strikeouts in both the fourth and fifth innings. Gabriel Moreno smacked his 12th home run leading off the fourth, a 387-foot drive to left-center, to smear Javier's line. Astros relievers Enyel De Los Santos, Bennett Sousa, Bryan Abreu and Hader preserved the lead. Abreu benefited from a nifty double play started by Pena in the eighth. The shortstop fielded a Marte grounder and tagged Moreno before he could scurry back to second. Pena had enough time to fire to first before Marte arrived. --Field Level Media

item.title: Seattle Times, Newsday sue OpenAI, Microsoft, alleging copyright infringement
item.description: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft on Friday, alleging in federal court that the tech companies copied the newspapers' journalism without permission to train their AI systems.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Seattle Times and Newsday sued OpenAI and Microsoft (MSFT.O) on Friday, alleging in federal court that the tech companies copied the newspapers' journalism without permission to train their AI systems. The suit in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York alleges that OpenAI and Microsoft scraped the newspapers' websites, including content behind paywalls, and incorporated articles into datasets used to train and operate products including ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot and Bing's AI features. The newspapers, based in Seattle and Long Island, New York, said the companies' AI products can reproduce passages from their reporting, closely paraphrase articles and provide users with answers that reduce the need to visit their websites or buy subscriptions. "We feel strongly that we must defend our content - which we spend millions of dollars a year to produce - from being used without our consent or compensation," Seattle Times President and CEO Alan Fisco wrote to employees, according to the newspaper. A spokesperson for San Francisco-based OpenAI said its models are trained on publicly available data and grounded in fair use, without commenting specifically on the lawsuit. A spokesperson for Microsoft, based near Seattle in Washington state, said in an email: "While we’re surprised by the lawsuit, we appreciate the importance of local journalism and we’re always happy to sit down and explore solutions to this type of dispute." The Seattle Times and Newsday are seeking an order requiring the destruction of copies of their works as well as training datasets or AI models incorporating them. The lawsuit echoes a case filed by [USN:L6N44U18K TEXT:"the New York Times"] (NYT.N) in 2023, which accused OpenAI and Microsoft (MSFT.O) of using millions of newspaper articles without permission to train OpenAI's popular chatbot. The case is ongoing, and is one of dozens brought by copyright holders against tech companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta for what they say is misuse of their material to train AI systems. (This story has been refiled to say 'a,' not 'an' spokesperson, in the fourth bullet point.)

item.title: Alejandro Kirk, Ernie Clement spark Blue Jays past Royals
item.description: Alejandro Kirk and Ernie Clement had two hits and a pair of RBIs apiece to help the visiting Toronto Blue Jays post a 9-2 victory over the Kansas City Royals on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Alejandro Kirk and Ernie Clement had two hits and a pair of RBIs apiece to help the visiting Toronto Blue Jays post a 9-2 victory over the Kansas City Royals on Friday. After Toronto (71-71) starter Jameson Taillon exited with elbow discomfort following two innings, four relievers combined to throw seven innings of one-run ball. Michael Lorenzen earned a rare three-inning save to close the door. George Springer also drove in two runs for the Blue Jays, who won their sixth game in seven tries, pulling within a half-game of the Cleveland Guardians for the third American League wild card slot. Daniel Lynch IV (4-5) allowed five runs on seven hits across five innings while walking one for the Royals (63-79), who have lost four of their last five. Bobby Witt Jr. and Vinnie Pasquantino bookended the loss with solo homers for Kansas City. Toronto jumped on Lynch early, as Brett Bateman was hit by a pitch and Vladimir Guerrero Jr. slashed a one-out single in the top of the first. Kirk and Kazuma Okamoto then lined consecutive RBI base hits to give the visitors a 2-0 edge. Two batters later, Clement hit his 30th double of the season to extend the first-inning margin to four. Witt helped cut into the deficit in the bottom of the first, as he connected on his 17th homer of the year -- a 410-foot solo shot. Myles Straw and Guerrero singled in the second, before Kirk drove in another run with a double to center. Taillon was relieved after the second inning by Joe Mantiply (2-0) who tossed two scoreless frames. Nolan Hoffman entered for Lynch in the sixth. The first Kansas City reliever was greeted with singles from Clement and Nathan Lukes and Straw's run-scoring sacrifice bunt. Brett Bateman then walked and Springer followed with a two-run double to make it 8-1. Rookie first baseman Sean Keys entered as a defensive replacement for Guerrero in the eighth before leading off the top of the ninth with his second major league homer off Kansas City reliever Easton McGee. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bolivie-Une explosion dans une caserne fait au moins 10 morts
item.description: Au moins dix personnes ont été tuées et des dizaines d'autres ont été blessées vendredi après une explosion dans une caserne militaire de la ville de Viacha, en Bolivie, ont dit les autorités locales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Au moins dix personnes ont été tuées et des dizaines d'autres ont été blessées vendredi après une explosion dans une caserne militaire de la ville de Viacha, en Bolivie, ont dit les autorités locales. L'explosion est survenue vers 14h30 (18h30 GMT) dans une zone utilisée pour stocker du matériel pyrotechnique, ont fait savoir les autorités. La cause de l'explosion doit encore être établie. Des responsables ont toutefois déclaré qu'elle s'était produite dans la réserve de feux d'artifice du ministère de la Défense. La directrice des services de santé de Viacha, Rita Nebraska, a dit à la télévision locale qu'il était estimé qu'entre dix et 15 personnes avait péri dans l'incident, et que 62 autres étaient blessées. Quatorze blessés ont été transportés dans un hôpital de La Paz, à quelque 30 kilomètres, pour y être soignés, a-t-elle précisé. La police a déclaré que plus de 50 personnes avaient été blessées et que des dizaines d'habitations avaient subi des dégâts. Rita Nebraska a dit que les pompiers avaient prévenus qu'une autre explosion était possible en raison de la chaleur sur place et qu'ils avaient appelé les habitants à se tenir à au moins 150 mètres du site.

item.title: Fifth-inning uprising rallies Brewers past Reds
item.description: Rookie Cooper Pratt ripped a bases-clearing triple and scored on a wild pitch during the fifth inning, lifting the visiting Milwaukee Brewers to a 10-7 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Rookie Cooper Pratt ripped a bases-clearing triple and scored on a wild pitch during the fifth inning, lifting the visiting Milwaukee Brewers to a 10-7 victory over the Cincinnati Reds on Friday. Milwaukee's Brice Turang had a two-run double among his three hits, drove in a run after being hit by a pitch with the bases loaded and also scored on a groundout. David Hamilton had an RBI triple and William Contreras added a run-scoring double for the Brewers (88-54), who own the majors' best record and have won seven of their last 10 games. Cincinnati's Eugenio Suarez belted a three-run homer in his return from a two-game absence in order to take the U.S. naturalization test. With his new walk-up song being Lee Greenwood's "God Bless The USA," the Venezuela-born Suarez deposited a 2-2 fastball from Shane Drohan over the wall in center field. The homer, which staked Cincinnati (67-74) to a 6-4 lead in the third, was the 21st of the season for Suarez and his third in six games. Milwaukee responded with a flourish by loading the bases against Rhett Lowder (6-9), who was relieved by Sam Moll. Turang was hit by a pitch, and Pratt followed with a bases-clearing triple down the right field line before scoring on a wild pitch to give the Brewers a 9-6 lead. Chad Patrick (8-4) relieved Drohan and allowed one hit over two scoreless innings. Drohan gave up six runs on five hits over four innings. Rookie Sal Stewart had an RBI single in the seventh to cut Milwaukee's lead to 10-7. Aaron Ashby fanned two in the eighth for the Brewers and Trevor Megill struck out the side in the ninth to secure his 26th save of the season. Lowder permitted seven runs (six earned) on six hits in four innings. Elly De La Cruz's RBI single to left field opened the scoring in the first before Milwaukee scratched for a pair of runs in the second, highlighted by Hamilton's RBI triple down the right field line. Matt McLain sent a 1-2 fastball from Drohan over the wall in left-center to give Cincinnati a 3-2 lead in the second. However, Turang's two-run double regained the lead for the Brewers in the third. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nolan McLean wins 3rd straight as Mets down Giants
item.description: Nolan McLean worked through six innings and won his third straight decision Friday night, when the host New York Mets beat the San Francisco Giants 10-6 in the opener of a three-game series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Nolan McLean worked through six innings and won his third straight decision Friday night, when the host New York Mets beat the San Francisco Giants 10-6 in the opener of a three-game series. Mark Vientos hit a three-run homer in the first to give the Mets (64-77) a lead they'd never relinquish. Francisco Alvarez went deep twice while Bo Bichette and Francisco Lindor each had two-run homers. Juan Soto hit into an RBI forceout for the Mets, who have won four of six. Lindor, Vientos, Alvarez and Bichette all finished with two hits apiece. Rafael Devers was 3-for-4 with five RBIs via a two-RBI double and a three-run homer, for the Giants (58-84), who have dropped three of four. Turner Hill finished 2-for-4 with a run-scoring single in the sixth. Jonah Cox had two hits and scored two runs after entering as a pinch-hitter in the seventh. McLean (11-8) allowed two runs on six hits and four walks while striking out seven. The rookie right-hander had just two 1-2-3 innings but limited the Giants to two hits in 11 plate appearances with runners in scoring position. He wriggled out of a bases-loaded, none-out jam in the fifth when McLean struck out Jung Hoo Lee before getting Drew Cavanaugh to hit into a double play. McLean is 3-0 with a 1.08 ERA in his last four starts. Jefry Yan and Austin Warren combined to give up four runs in 1 2/3 innings. Warren surrendered Devers' blast with two outs in the eighth before Robert Stock, who made his first six appearances this season as a starter, recorded the final out. Alvarez's second homer in the bottom of the inning removed the save situation for Kodai Senga, who threw a hitless ninth. Rookie Matt Wilkinson (0-3) took the loss for the Giants after giving up seven runs (four earned) on five hits and two walks while striking out two over three innings. Yunior Marte went the rest of the way and allowed three runs on four hits and two walks while striking out two. --Field Level Media

item.title: Shota Imanaga leads Cubs past Marlins into top wild-card spot
item.description: Shota Imanaga outdueled Janson Junk on Friday to lead the Chicago Cubs to a 6-1 win over the host Miami Marlins.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Shota Imanaga outdueled Janson Junk on Friday to lead the Chicago Cubs to a 6-1 win over the host Miami Marlins. The Cubs won their second straight game and took over the top spot in the National League wild-card standings, thanks to their starter. The Cubs' left-hander dominated the Marlins, pitching into the seventh inning for the first time since July 31. Imanaga (9-10) allowed one run on three hits and no walks over six-plus innings. He departed after Griffin Conine led off the seventh with a hard-hit single. Conine (2-for-4) scored on an Esteury Ruiz fielder's choice in the seventh. Cubs batters took advantage of Marlins relievers' wildness, scoring three runs in the sixth and another in the seventh. Jack Ralston walked three of the four batters he faced, and Josh Ekness followed by allowing another walk and two hits, as the Cubs broke open a one-run game. Only 12 of their 34 pitches were strikes in the decisive sixth. Prior to that, Junk (6-9) nearly matched Imanaga over five innings. He allowed three hits and a walk, with the only run coming on a Pedro Ramirez fielder's choice in the second inning. Junk retired 11 of the last 12 batters he faced. Nico Hoerner went 3-for-4 with an RBI. Alex Bregman extended his hitting streak to eight thanks to a 2-for-4 night with a walk and a run scored and Michael Busch (1-for-4) added a ninth-inning solo home run, his 18th of the season. Pete Crow-Armstrong (1-for-3, two runs and a stolen base) started the seventh with a double and eventually scored on a Bradley Blalock wild pitch. The Cubs center fielder also made a highlight-reel catch, leaping at the left-center field wall to rob Heriberto Hernandez of an extra-base hit in the sixth. Aaron Civale, who relieved Imanaga in the seventh, suffered from some wildness as well. He allowed two two-out walks to load the bases in the inning but got pinch hitter Joe Mack looking at a curveball that dropped into the strike zone to end the threat. Civale then retired the last six batters in order to earn his second save of the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: US embassy issues health alert for Cuba amid oil blockade, sanctions
item.description: The U.S. embassy in Havana issued a health alert for Cuba on Friday, warning travelers and residents of a spike in intestinal illnesses and diarrhea caused by failing water and electricity supply, even as the Trump administration continued to hold back fuel shipments necessary for power generation on the island.
item.dc:creator: Dave Sherwood
item.content:encoded: The U.S. embassy in Havana issued a health alert for Cuba on Friday, warning travelers and residents of a spike in intestinal illnesses and diarrhea caused by failing water and electricity supply, even as the Trump administration continued to hold back fuel shipments necessary for power generation on the island. "The U.S. Embassy has noted a significant increase in diarrheal illness across Cuba, associated with the continuing degradation of the water and energy infrastructure," the alert stated. "This degradation affects water supply, and food storage and temperature control." The U.S. warning comes nine months after the Trump administration imposed a fuel blockade on the communist-run island, contributing to a sharp spike in power cuts and complicating refrigeration and sanitary measures in homes and businesses. U.N.-appointed human rights experts have called the Trump fuel blockade a violation of international law. A team of [USN:S8N41J077 TEXT:"U.N. experts"] in August warned of a growing risk of disease outbreaks on the island as the U.S. has tightened sanctions. "The humanitarian consequences are already unfolding into a full-blown crisis, threatening the rights to health, to life, to food and to development," the experts said. The Trump administration says sanctions are necessary to force a change in the island's government, a decades-long aim of the U.S. following Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution. Trump has called Cuba a national security threat to the United States. Residents throughout Cuba have for months complained of rampant illnesses that cause several days of diarrhea, fever and body aches, leaving many bedridden. During the Caribbean's sultry summer, sleep without air conditioning or a fan often becomes impossible, as does food preservation without refrigeration. Blackouts spanning days have become commonplace amid the U.S. fuel blockade. The U.S. health alert on Friday advised travelers and residents in Cuba to "be cautious of ... perishable foods that may have been inadequately stored," and warned against eating "foods that appear to have been sitting at room temperature for extended periods."

item.title: White Sox ride trio of homers to victory over Twins
item.description: Colson Montgomery went 1-for-4 with a two-run home run, and the Chicago White Sox pulled away for a 4-1 win over the visiting Minnesota Twins on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Colson Montgomery went 1-for-4 with a two-run home run, and the Chicago White Sox pulled away for a 4-1 win over the visiting Minnesota Twins on Friday night. Miguel Vargas and Braden Montgomery each hit solo homers for Chicago (74-67) in the opener of a three-game series. The AL Central-leading White Sox ended a two-game skid. Josh Bell went 2-for-3 and homered to mark the lone run for Minnesota (67-74). Kody Clemens finished 3-for-4 for the Twins, who have dropped back-to-back games after winning three in a row. White Sox right-hander Erick Fedde (8-8) defeated the Twins for the second time in less than a week. He held Minnesota to three hits in five scoreless innings, walked two and struck out two. Twins right-hander Zebby Matthews (9-9) surrendered all four runs on four hits in five innings. He walked one and struck out four. The defeat marked the first time in six starts that Matthews did not earn a victory. The White Sox struck quickly in the bottom of the first inning. Matthews fired a fastball low and away, and Vargas took it the opposite direction for a homer to right-center field. The blast marked Vargas' 30th home run of the season. His previous high was 16, which he set with the White Sox in 2025. Braden Montgomery made it 2-0 with a blast in the second. He ripped a line-drive home run 419 feet to right-center field. The power surge continued in the fourth as the White Sox increased their lead to 4-0. After Andrew Benintendi drew a one-out walk, Colson Montgomery hammered a towering, 416-foot homer into the right-center-field bleachers for his 30th of the season. His previous career high was 21, set last year as a rookie. Bell put the Twins on the scoreboard in the ninth. He took right-hander Grant Taylor deep to right-center field for his 18th homer of the season. Bell's homer and a double by Royce Lewis marked the Twins' only extra-base hits. --Field Level Media

item.title: Chris Mueller, who once recorded brace for USMNT, retires
item.description: Marking the end of an eventful career, Chicago Fire FC winger Chris Mueller announced his retirement from professional soccer on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Marking the end of an eventful career, Chicago Fire FC winger Chris Mueller announced his retirement from professional soccer on Friday. Mueller made an impression in two caps for the U.S. Men's National Team. He recorded a brace in the USMNT's 6-0 win over El Salvador in a friendly in 2020. Mueller was diagnosed with pericarditis in 2025, which cost him the season. He returned for the Fire in February, making his debut in a preseason friendly against the LA Galaxy. He appeared in five regular-season games with one start. "Goodbyes are never easy, especially when you're waving farewell to a game you've centered the last 20 years of your life around," Mueller said in a statement provided to the Fire. "With that being said, this has been a decision that hasn't come without real challenge, a hefty amount of consideration, and serious contemplation." Mueller, 30, is a native of Illinois and joined the Fire in 2022, fulfilling a lifelong dream of suiting up for his childhood club. In 66 appearances over the next five seasons, Mueller tallied six goals and 10 assists. "Thank you to the Chicago Fire, firstly, for bringing me home and allowing me to play for my childhood club," Mueller said. "And secondly, but more importantly, for their support throughout me battling through this diagnosis. Truly, it was unbelievable and I never felt alone in it. "I'm beyond excited to see where the Club continues to head and for the victories that are yet to come. Thank you, Chicago. A supporter, I will always be." Prior to joining Chicago, Mueller had stints with Orlando City (2018-21) and Hibernian F.C. of the Scottish Premiership (2022). His four-year run with Orlando resulted in 21 goals and 24 assists in 112 appearances. --Field Level Media

item.title: Jared Jones fans 9 as Pirates blank Angels
item.description: Jared Jones matched his season high with nine strikeouts over six three-hit innings and Jake Mangum had an RBI double to lead the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 1-0 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Angels in the opener of a three-game series on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jared Jones matched his season high with nine strikeouts over six three-hit innings and Jake Mangum had an RBI double to lead the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 1-0 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Angels in the opener of a three-game series on Friday night. Bryan Reynolds also doubled and had two hits for Pittsburgh (70-72), which won for the fifth time in its last six games. Konnor Griffin, activated off the 60-day injured list after missing 49 games with a torn sagittal band in his left ring finger, scored the lone run of the contest. Jones (3-6) walked one while snapping a seven-start winless drought dating back to a 7-1 victory at Cleveland on July 18. He left after throwing a season-high 91 pitches, 63 for strikes. Wilber Dotel followed Jones, recording two strikeouts and a walk over two innings, setting the stage for Mason Montgomery, who pitched around a leadoff single by Mike Trout in the ninth to pick up his ninth save. Ryan Johnson (3-8) suffered the loss for Los Angeles (53-88) despite allowing just one run on four hits in six innings. He walked two and struck out six. Pittsburgh scored the game's only run in the bottom of the second. Oneil Cruz led off with a walk but was erased at second on a fielder's choice by Griffin. Mangum then doubled into the right field corner, driving in Griffin, who barely beat the relay throw to the plate and avoided a sweeping tag attempt by catcher Moises Ballesteros with a headfirst slide. Pittsburgh missed a chance to extend its lead in the eighth inning when it loaded the bases. Spencer Horwitz walked, advanced to second on Reynolds' single, and went to third when Nick Gonzales was hit by a pitch. But Angels reliever Samy Natera Jr. struck out Cruz to end the threat. The Angels' best chance to tie it came in the ninth when Trout led off with a single to right. However, Wade Meckler popped out trying to sacrifice, Vaughn Grissom flew out to the warning track in right and Montgomery then struck out pinch-hitter Travis d'Arnaud to end the game. --Field Level Media

item.title: White House reviews candidates to replace Hegseth deputy Feinberg, sources say
item.description: The White House has reviewed candidates to potentially replace Deputy Secretary of Defense Steve Feinberg, three people familiar with the discussions told Reuters, a sign that more leadership change could come for a Pentagon already facing unusually high staff turnover.
item.dc:creator: Mike Stone, Erin Banco, David Jeans
item.content:encoded: The White House has reviewed candidates to potentially replace Deputy Secretary of Defense Steve Feinberg, three people familiar with the discussions told Reuters, a sign that more leadership change could come for a Pentagon already facing unusually high staff turnover. The effort, which was under way in June, has included conversations with senior lawmakers in the Senate about whether the administration's picks would have enough support to be confirmed, said two of the people, one of whom added that the review was still going on as of late August. Reuters could not determine when the White House began considering candidates. The three sources said no decision had been made to remove Feinberg from his post. They did not say why the White House was reviewing potential replacements and did not specify which candidates the White House was considering. "These so-called anonymous 'sources' have no idea what they are talking about," said White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly. "President Trump appreciates the work of Secretary Hegseth, Deputy Secretary Feinberg, and the entire Department of War, whose record of success in Operation Epic Fury, Operation Absolute Resolve, and Operation Midnight Hammer speaks for itself," she said, referring to U.S. military operations in Iran and Venezuela. The Pentagon denied a process was under way to replace Feinberg. Asked for comment by Reuters, Hegseth said in a statement that Feinberg has his full support and “isn’t going anywhere.” The Pentagon did not provide a comment from Feinberg and declined to make him available for an interview. A departure by Feinberg, the billionaire co-founder of private equity firm Cerberus Capital Management, would be the most senior staff change for a department that has already seen a string of high-profile departures under Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll resigned this week following months of tension with Hegseth, according to a source familiar with the matter. The Army has declined to comment on the reasons for his departure. Navy Secretary John Phelan and several senior Army leaders have also departed in recent months. Feinberg, who vowed to accelerate U.S. munitions production, has not yet met that goal, according to analysts who say that the U.S. industrial base cannot ramp up quickly. Some defense industry executives say his task has been complicated by the slow pace of Congress appropriating funds despite [USN:L1N42V0TF TEXT:"immense pressure"] from the administration. Feinberg "has worked tirelessly to rebuild our Defense Industrial Base and ensure our military has everything it needs to win, and I look forward to continuing to work with him," Hegseth said in his statement to Reuters, adding, "He’s doing a tremendous job for President Trump, for the Department, and for our warfighters." FRUSTRATION OVER THE IRAN WAR Trump has increasingly expressed frustration with the lack of progress in the six-month-old Iran war, which has settled into a costly standoff between the U.S. and Iran. One of the costs has been a drawdown of U.S. weapons stockpiles. Reuters has reported that the U.S. military faces [USN:L1N4410KB TEXT:"significant shortages"] of certain munitions, which have alarmed Congress and military leaders. Trump has dismissed the concerns, saying the U.S. has "far more munitions than anyone in the world." But in an exchange with Trump at Camp David earlier this month, according to the Washington Post, Hegseth blamed Feinberg for letting stockpiles of long-range guided missiles and air-defense interceptors shrink. The White House has called the report "fake news." In a statement to Reuters, chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said: "Secretary Hegseth did not mislead anyone about our munitions posture, and he did not blame Deputy Secretary Feinberg." Appointed by Trump last year, Feinberg has attempted to reshape the Pentagon by ramping up the U.S. military's direct investments in companies and delivering loans to military contractors through multiple offices inside the department, including the Office of Strategic Capital and the newly created Economic Defense Unit. In an August 18 memo he sent to defense firms and seen by Reuters, Feinberg called on contractors to speed up production and provide more transparency around pricing. The Pentagon did not respond to a question about the memo. Feinberg has also come under scrutiny on Capitol Hill, where Democratic U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren has raised concerns about whether his former firm Cerberus could benefit from the Pentagon's spending on its Golden Dome missile defense program. “There are no conflicts of interest between Deputy Secretary of War Steve Feinberg and Cerberus," said Parnell. "He has completely divested from Cerberus and has recused himself from any conversations or business relationships between the Executive Branch and Cerberus." Cerberus did not respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Ranger Suarez tosses 7 innings as Red Sox shut out Orioles
item.description: Ranger Suarez fired seven sharp innings and Mickey Gasper homered in the first, lifting the Boston Red Sox to a 1-0 victory against the host Baltimore Orioles on Friday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Ranger Suarez fired seven sharp innings and Mickey Gasper homered in the first, lifting the Boston Red Sox to a 1-0 victory against the host Baltimore Orioles on Friday night. Suarez (6-4) limited the Orioles to five hits and one walk while striking out three across a 91-pitch effort. He won for just the second time in his past nine starts. Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman each pitched an inning in relief to complete the shutout. Chapman notched his 32nd save, and second in as many nights, by working the ninth. The Red Sox (77-65) earned their second victory in a row, but only their fourth in a 10-game stretch. The Orioles (69-73) took a fourth consecutive loss. Gasper had two of Boston's five hits. Orioles starter Shane Baz (5-15) lasted 6 1/3 innings, yielding one run on four hits and two walks. He struck out six in an unsuccessful bid for a second straight win following an 0-8 run in a 12-start stretch. Blaze Alexander registered three of Baltimore's six hits, which were all singles. The Orioles left six runners on base but had only three batters go to the plate with a runner in scoring position. Boston stranded 10 runners, going 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position. Gasper was the game's second batter and he homered on a first-pitch fastball. His eighth long ball of the season was the only extra-base hit in the game. The Red Sox threatened by loading the bases with two outs in the seventh inning on a single, a walk and a hit batter. However, reliever Alex Hoppe retired Adley Rutschman, the ex-Oriole who homered twice on Thursday in the series opener, on a flyout to end the scoring chance. Josh Walker and Cam Sanders each pitched a shutout inning in relief for Baltimore, which would need to win the next two games in order to split the four-game series. --Field Level Media

item.title: Trump grants clemency to 30 people, White House pardon czar says
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump granted clemency this week to 30 people, including Emory Jones, a longtime associate of rap mogul Jay-Z, White House "pardon czar" Alice Marie Johnson posted on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. President Donald Trump granted clemency this week to 30 people, including Emory Jones, a longtime associate of rap mogul Jay-Z, White House "pardon czar" Alice Marie Johnson posted on Friday. Jones served nearly 16 years in federal prison on drug charges, Johnson wrote in a social media post announcing the clemency actions. The president took the action on Thursday, according to Johnson, the White House official responsible for organizing clemency efforts. Jones was released in 2010 after Jay-Z wrote a letter to a judge on his behalf, seeking a sentence reduction. Jones has worked as an executive at Jay-Z's Roc Nation entertainment company and co-founded the Paper Planes clothing brand. The New York Times reported that other clemency recipients include a former Philadelphia union boss convicted of bribery and an ex-Navy sailor imprisoned for firearms offenses. Trump has granted pardons of criminal convictions and commutations shortening sentences for [USN:L6N42H19B TEXT:"more than 1,700"] people since his second White House term began in January 2025.

item.title: Chris Sale, Braves top Cristopher Sanchez, Phils, boost NL East lead
item.description: Chris Sale outdueled Cristopher Sanchez in a battle of aces and Mauricio Dubon hit a late two-run homer as the visiting Atlanta Braves topped the Philadelphia Phillies 5-2 on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Chris Sale outdueled Cristopher Sanchez in a battle of aces and Mauricio Dubon hit a late two-run homer as the visiting Atlanta Braves topped the Philadelphia Phillies 5-2 on Friday. Sale (14-9) allowed two runs and six hits in six innings, striking out seven and walking one. Sanchez (16-5) also tossed six innings, giving up three runs, five hits and three walks while fanning five. Ronald Acuna Jr. had an RBI single as part of a 3-for-5 night for Atlanta, which earned its ninth win in 11 games. Alec Bohm produced a solo homer and an RBI double for Philadelphia, which took its second straight loss after a six-game winning streak. Bryce Harper had his career-high on-base streak end at 35 games. The Braves (84-57) increased their lead to five games over the second-place Phillies (79-62) in the National League East. The teams will play three more games in the current series, then three in Atlanta the following weekend. Sanchez worked around a leadoff baserunner in the first inning, but he wasn't as fortunate in the following frame. Lane Thomas opened the second with a walk and advanced on Dubon's base hit. Two batters later, Austin Riley delivered an RBI single. After a run-scoring groundout from Ha-Seong Kim, Acuna lined a base hit into center to put the visitors ahead 3-0. Philadelphia promptly got one run back when Luis Arraez opened the bottom of the second with a single and Bohm hit the next pitch into left for an RBI double. Bohm was back in the mix again in the fourth, lining a first-pitch fastball from Sale over the fence in left field to get the hosts within 3-2. The Phillies had runners on second and third with two outs in the fifth, but Sale induced Harper into an inning-ending popout. Sanchez concluded his night with a strikeout of Riley on his 108th pitch of the night, ending the sixth inning. Atlanta added a pair of insurance runs in the eighth. Pinch hitter Mike Yastrzemski drew a one-out walk against Orion Kerkering before Dubon lifted a two-run homer to left-center, making it 5-2. Raisel Iglesias was glad to accept the additional buffer, as the Atlanta closer struck out two in a perfect ninth inning for his 30th save. --Field Level Media

item.title: Explosion at Bolivia military base kills at least 10, dozens injured
item.description: At least 10 people were killed and dozens more injured on Friday after an explosion at a military barracks in the Bolivian municipality of Viacha, about 30 km (19 miles) from La Paz, local authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: At least 10 people were killed and dozens more injured on Friday after an explosion at a military barracks in the Bolivian municipality of Viacha, about 30 km (19 miles) from La Paz, local authorities said. The blast occurred at around 2:30 p.m. (1830 GMT) local time in an area used to store pyrotechnic material, authorities said. While the cause has yet to be established, officials said the blast originated from the defense ministry's fireworks stockpile. Viacha health director Rita Nebraska told local television that between 10 and 15 people were believed to have died in the incident, while 62 people were injured. Fourteen of the wounded were transferred to hospitals in La Paz, including a girl with third-degree burns, she said. Police said more than 50 people were injured and dozens of homes damaged, largely by windows shattered in the blast. Ambulances, medical teams and police were deployed to the military complex to assess the damage and evacuate the wounded to health centers. Nebraska said firefighters had warned that a heat source remained at the site, raising the risk of another explosion, and urged residents to stay at least 150 meters away.

item.title: Charlie Woods shoots 71, sits 4 back at Junior Players
item.description: Charlie Woods put himself in contention at the Junior Players Championship on Friday, firing a 1-under-par 71 at TPC Sawgrass in Ponte Vedra Beach, Fla.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Charlie Woods put himself in contention at the Junior Players Championship on Friday, firing a 1-under-par 71 at TPC Sawgrass in Ponte Vedra Beach, Fla. The 17-year-old recorded five birdies and four bogeys on the par-72 Stadium Course in his lowest competitive round at the venue where his father, Tiger Woods, twice won the Players Championship. Charlie Woods was tied for eighth when he finished shortly before 2 p.m. ET, minutes before weather halted play. After the round was completed, he was tied for ninth, four strokes behind leader Chase Bauer, who shot a 5-under 67. Starting on the back nine, Woods overcame bogeys at Nos. 11 and 14 with consecutive birdies at Nos. 15 and 16. His most memorable escape came one hole later at the famous par-3 17th. Woods pulled his tee shot toward the left side of the island green and initially thought the ball had gone into the water. Instead, it stayed dry on the footpath leading onto the green. Faced with little room, Woods chipped to approximately 4 feet and converted the par putt. "I was pleasantly surprised," Woods said of discovering his tee shot hadn't found the water. He then rolled in an 18-foot birdie putt at No. 18 to make the turn at 1 under. Woods added birdies at Nos. 3 and 9 while mixing in two more bogeys over his final nine holes. Friday's 71 continued a steady improvement for Woods at TPC Sawgrass. He tied for 31st at the event last year after rounds of 76, 75 and 72. Tiger Woods won the Players Championship at the Stadium Course in 2001 and again in 2013. His first victory featured the famous 60-foot birdie putt at No. 17 in the third round. Charlie Woods is scheduled to begin the second round from the first tee Saturday morning. --Field Level Media

item.title: CVC Corp renegocia dívida e alonga vencimentos até 2029
item.description: A CVC Corp anunciou nesta sexta-feira uma operação de renegociação de sua dívida, que prevê a redução do custo financeiro, alongamento de vencimentos e diminuição das saídas de caixa previstas para os próximos 12 meses.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A CVC Corp anunciou nesta sexta-feira uma operação de renegociação de sua dívida, que prevê a redução do custo financeiro, alongamento de vencimentos e diminuição das saídas de caixa previstas para os próximos 12 meses. A companhia possui aproximadamente R$400 milhões em dívida e já recebeu manifestações de intenção de cerca de R$200 milhões para adesão às novas condições, disse o grupo de agências de viagem em nota. Com a nova estrutura anunciada, a remuneração das debêntures passa de um spread com CDI +4,5% para CDI +3,9%, enquanto os vencimentos, que atualmente estão concentrados em outubro de 2026 e abril de 2027, passarão para março e setembro de 2029. Com isso, a companhia prevê efeitos sobre o fluxo de caixa. A CVC Corp disse que teria aproximadamente R$115 milhões em pagamentos previstos em outubro, considerando cerca de R$80 milhões de principal e R$35 milhões de juros. Para os debenturistas que aderirem à nova estrutura, a companhia disse que os juros serão incorporados ao principal e haverá amortização de 75% do valor original, reduzindo a necessidade de desembolso da companhia no quarto trimestre deste ano. Para abril de 2027, a previsão é uma redução do desembolso de aproximadamente R$110 milhões nas condições atuais para cerca de R$25 milhões. Considerados os efeitos da operação nos próximos 12 meses, a CVC Corp estima uma redução de aproximadamente R$110 milhões nas saídas de caixa. A nova estrutura também prevê o reforço das garantias vinculadas à operação, com os boletos dados em garantia aos debenturistas passando dos atuais R$72 milhões para aproximadamente R$130 milhões. "Fazer isso em um cenário econômico ainda desafiador demonstra a confiança dos nossos parceiros financeiros e nos dá ainda mais flexibilidade para seguir executando a estratégia da companhia", disse Felipe Gomes, diretor financeiro da CVC Corp.

item.title: Kennedy acknowledges one measles death in Pennsylvania
item.description: U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr acknowledged on Friday that measles caused the recent death of an infant in Pennsylvania, citing information from a county coroner, but suggested the federal government would not yet recognize the fatality in official data amid a fast-growing national outbreak.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: U.S. Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr acknowledged on Friday that measles caused the recent death of an infant in Pennsylvania, citing information from a county coroner, but suggested the federal government would not yet recognize the fatality in official data amid a fast-growing national outbreak. Last month, Kennedy asked for [USN:L6N44U1B7 TEXT:"two measles-related deaths"] reported by Pennsylvania’s health department to be removed from the CDC’s national tally of measles, questioning whether the virus was the cause, Reuters reported. CDC staffers had already accepted the state’s characterization of the deaths as linked to measles before Kennedy's request. Public health experts said the move amounted to extraordinary political interference in the authority of a state health department and an effort to minimize the risks of the highly infectious virus. Kennedy posted on X on Friday that he was relying on information from the coroner in Lancaster County, Pennsylvania, where the two deaths occurred. “The Lancaster County Coroner has now publicly stated that measles caused only the second infant’s death and has also publicly stated that the infant had Amish lethal microcephaly,” Kennedy wrote on X. He said that babies with that condition typically live about 6 months and the infant was approximately 2-months-old at death. The Lancaster coroner rejected the determination of the statewide health department that a second infant also died from measles, Kennedy said. Kennedy said the CDC's health statistics agency still needed to receive and review records on measles deaths. At the moment, the national data does not reflect any measles deaths in 2026, he said. The CDC updated its website on Friday with a note explaining that it was re-evaluating how it classified measles deaths. "This work is intended to promote consistent classification and reporting of measles deaths across jurisdictions,” the CDC website said without providing details on why reevaluation was required. A spokesperson for the Health and Human Services Department, which oversees CDC, did not immediately respond to questions about recording either of the Pennsylvania deaths. Neil Ruhland, a spokesman for the Pennsylvania Department of Health, reiterated on Friday that the state had confirmed two measles-related deaths in the state’s outbreak. He did not provide details on the deaths or comment on Kennedy’s remarks. The Lancaster coroner's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. U.S. measles cases have hit their highest level in more than three decades under President Donald Trump and Kennedy, his top health official and a long-time anti-vaccine activist. Kennedy has promoted the idea that vaccines, including the combined measles, mumps and rubella shot, are more dangerous than the diseases they prevent, despite decades of scientific evidence that the shots save lives. Leading medical organizations say that Kennedy’s statements about vaccines and his policies as health secretary, including efforts to reduce the number of government-recommended childhood immunizations, have increased vaccine hesitancy, making outbreaks harder to curb.

item.title: Court ruling temporarily restores eligibility for 2 Indiana defensive linemen
item.description: A pair of key Indiana defensive linemen are eligible to play in Saturday's season opener after a state court temporarily blocked the NCAA and Big Ten from keeping them off the field.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A pair of key Indiana defensive linemen are eligible to play in Saturday's season opener after a state court temporarily blocked the NCAA and Big Ten from keeping them off the field. Monroe Circuit Court Judge Kara Krothe issued a temporary restraining order Friday, restoring eligibility for Stephen Daley and Kellan Wyatt, as well as six other college athletes who challenged NCAA rules that prevented them from competing during the 2026-27 academic year. The ruling means Daley and Wyatt can rejoin No. 6 Indiana when the defending national champion opens its season at home against North Texas. Krothe wrote that the athletes should be returned to the positions they held following their most recent college seasons, provided they would otherwise have qualified to compete with an additional year of eligibility. "As long as they would have been eligible, academically and otherwise, to continue playing college sports in the following semester if they had a fifth year of eligibility, they are eligible today," Krothe wrote. A hearing on the athletes' requests for a preliminary injunction is scheduled for Sept. 11, meaning Friday's ruling does not permanently settle the dispute. Daley and Wyatt initially returned to Indiana in August, before their eligibility was once again called into question. On Aug. 21, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th Circuit stayed a separate ruling that had granted another season of eligibility to qualifying athletes from the high school Class of 2022 who were excluded from the NCAA's new eligibility framework. Both players were important pieces of Indiana's defense during its 16-0 championship season. Daley recorded 19 tackles for loss, 5.5 sacks and two forced fumbles in 13 games. A knee injury suffered in the postgame celebration following Indiana's 13-10 victory over Ohio State in the Big Ten championship game kept him out of the College Football Playoff. Wyatt started seven games before a knee injury against Michigan State ended his season. He finished with eight tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks. The other plaintiffs include Miami basketball player Malik Reneau; Indiana volleyball player Avry Tatum; Butler basketball player Yohan Traore; defensive back Jordan Johnson, who intends to play at Purdue, and Indiana swimmers Owen McDonald and Zalan Sarkany. --Field Level Media

item.title: Deputado do partido governista mexicano é encontrado morto com ferimento à bala
item.description: Um deputado federal do partido Morena, atualmente no poder no México, foi encontrado nesta sexta-feira morto com um ferimento à bala no Estado de Veracruz, no leste do país, a menos de um ano das eleições locais e federais.
item.dc:creator: Lizbeth Diaz
item.content:encoded: Um deputado federal do partido Morena, atualmente no poder no México, foi encontrado nesta sexta-feira morto com um ferimento à bala no Estado de Veracruz, no leste do país, a menos de um ano das eleições locais e federais. Zenyazen Escobar, parlamentar federal que representava o Estado litorâneo onde se encontram alguns dos complexos petrolíferos do país, foi encontrado morto dentro de seu carro com pelo menos um ferimento à bala. “O inquérito está sendo montado”, disse a procuradora-geral do Estado, Lisbeth Jiménez, sem fornecer detalhes. O secretário-geral de Veracruz, Ricardo Ahued, afirmou que o veículo do parlamentar não apresentava sinais de violência. A Câmara dos Deputados do México expressou suas condolências à família e aos amigos de Escobar e instou autoridades a conduzirem uma “investigação minuciosa dos fatos”. A morte ocorreu enquanto o país se prepara para eleições, em 6 de junho, para renovar cargos de prefeito, deputado estadual, vereador e governador. Em eleições anteriores, diversas regiões sofreram incidentes de violência ligados a grupos do crime organizado que buscavam cooptar figuras políticas e consolidar o controle territorial. De acordo com a organização de direitos humanos Data Cívica, somente em julho ocorreram pelo menos 30 incidentes de “violência político-criminal” em 11 Estados do México, sendo 14 deles homicídios. Os Estados com o maior número de casos registrados foram Zacatecas, com 10 casos; Michoacán e Quintana Roo, com quatro cada; Oaxaca, com três; e Baixa Califórnia e Veracruz, com dois cada. A Data Cívica descreve a violência político-criminal como ameaças, homicídios, ataques armados, tentativas de assassinato, desaparecimentos e sequestros. O órgão eleitoral nacional, o INE, alertou que o crime organizado representa uma das preocupações mais sérias para os processos democráticos. Segundo o INE, decisões judiciais já documentaram, no passado, a presença de indivíduos armados com o objetivo de intimidar ou coagir o público a votar de determinada maneira, assim como atos de furto e incêndio de material eleitoral.

item.title: Equador diz que afundamento de embarcações pelos EUA fazia parte de investigação conjunta contra tráfico de drogas
item.description: O Equador defendeu nesta sexta-feira as operações dos EUA que interceptaram e afundaram três embarcações equatorianas nesta semana, enquanto parentes de alguns tripulantes afirmaram que os homens eram pescadores e acusaram Washington de agir sem provas.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Valencia, Yury Garcia
item.content:encoded: O Equador defendeu nesta sexta-feira as operações dos EUA que interceptaram e afundaram três embarcações equatorianas nesta semana, enquanto parentes de alguns tripulantes afirmaram que os homens eram pescadores e acusaram Washington de agir sem provas. O episódio é o mais recente de uma campanha cada vez mais ampla dos EUA contra o tráfico marítimo de drogas no Pacífico oriental, que tem gerado críticas de grupos de direitos humanos e preocupação na América Latina quanto ao uso de força letal no mar. Os familiares contestaram a versão oficial. A esposa de um tripulante, que se identificou como Rosalba, de 47 anos, sem revelar o sobrenome, disse por telefone que os homens estavam pescando quando foram abordados e que nenhuma droga foi encontrada. “Não entendo por que o governo dos EUA tem que agir de forma tão arbitrária”, disse ela, acusando-o de violar os direitos humanos dos pescadores. Ela afirmou que a embarcação transportava apenas peixes e alegou que foi atingida em águas equatorianas, e não internacionais. A Reuters não conseguiu verificar de forma independente a versão dela. O governo do Equador afirmou que a operação foi resultado de investigações conjuntas com Washington, visando a logística do contrabando de drogas ligada a gangues criminosas. “Este é um trabalho realizado por meio da cooperação internacional”, disse o ministro do Interior, John Reimberg, à emissora Teleamazonas, acrescentando que as embarcações serviam como pontos flutuantes de reabastecimento que ajudavam lanchas a transportar drogas para o norte, em direção ao México e aos Estados Unidos. O Comando Sul dos EUA afirmou que as embarcações afundadas nesta semana estavam sendo usadas como postos de reabastecimento para o tráfico de drogas e disse que elas estavam ligadas à gangue Los Choneros. Um vídeo divulgado pelos militares mostrou imagens em preto e branco de agentes se aproximando e abordando uma embarcação antes de ela ser explodida no mar. A Reuters não conseguiu verificar de forma independente a data e o local das imagens. A Marinha do Equador informou que 28 tripulantes de duas embarcações — nove do Conquista 2 e 19 do OM2 — chegaram a Manta às 15h (horário local), a bordo de uma embarcação da guarda costeira. Outros oito tripulantes do Conquista 2 ainda estavam retornando ao porto a bordo de outra embarcação.

item.title: Niger blames France for inciting soldiers' mutiny
item.description: Niger has blamed France for inciting an attack on a key military airbase by mutinous soldiers last week, according to a government statement read on TV on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Niger has blamed France for inciting an attack on a key military airbase by mutinous soldiers last week, according to a government statement read on TV on Friday. Mutinous soldiers in the West African country attacked the airport and the presidency in the capital, Niamey, [USN:L1N44Q00F TEXT:"on August 29"], the latest threat to the rule of Abdourahamane Tiani, who seized power in a 2023 coup. Explosions and gunfire also rang out at a military airbase, but Niger's army, backed by Russian paramilitary forces, regained control over it the next day. The Council of Ministers on Friday concluded that the attack had been incited by a vast network of accomplices led by France, according to the statement. "A substantial body of evidence has been compiled regarding this attack, and Niger reserves the right to bring the matter before international courts," the government said in the statement. The attack highlighted tensions within Niger's armed forces, which have suffered repeated battlefield losses while fighting a jihadist insurgency. Tiani blamed France and other West African countries for unrest in the capital [USN:L1N3YU00A TEXT:"earlier this year"], without providing evidence.

The Phillies didn't immediately provide a reason for Stott's removal. However, Stott and his wife, Dru, announced in May that Dru would be giving birth to a girl in September. Stott was slated to bat seventh and play third base. Edmundo Sosa moved from left field to third and Bryan De La Cruz started in left and batted seventh against Braves starter Chris Sale.
